title: Anthropic launches Claude Duet as Meta's Muse passes 10 million users
summary: Meta's Muse passes ten million users with shopping as a top use, and Anthropic answers with Claude Duet, a background agent for small-business work that won't move money even if you approve it. Then how fifty thousand words of drift got an older Claude model to draft a voter-suppression plan, the PHP2Shell patch scramble, and a startup screwing sensors into trees.

topics: Meta Muse passes 10M users (Q3 earnings call, 21 October 2026; Sensor Tower via TechCrunch, 20 October): 10.9M downloads in first 40 days, 10.2M US; one of 12 apps to hit 10M US downloads that fast; first-40-day US downloads ChatGPT 3.7M, Grok 500k, Claude 200k; Meta put 39% of its October ad spend on Muse (23% in September); US retention 30% day 7 / 23% day 14 vs rival average 19%/16%; ~25% of people who set it up use it daily; over a quarter of engaged users who shopped averaged purchases above $200; Plaid connector activity unprecedented per Zuckerberg; plan: free for most, take a cut of commerce, charge power users; Muse Secure VM, Confidential VM coming; >10x cost-efficiency target within a year; 'Muse network' and talking to a business's agent instead of its website. Walmart Agent Gateway (MCP server) and Agent Profiles (next month, per-agent profile, approval or spending limit, returns apply when the agent errs). On air: Alan's nested-denominator objection to the shopping stat; Alan recalled his 7 October position that Muse was the bigger story because the memory is the product.

Claude Duet (research preview, 21 October 2026): separate app on iOS/Android/claude.ai, waitlist for US Pro and Max, built around Opus 5.5; morning brief, checks connected accounts about every few hours partly to conserve usage limits; runs on a VM with its own browser; 6,000+ marketplace connectors; aimed at professionals and small business owners, personal tasks weaker; approval before sending, paying, signing or deleting; trading securities and moving money between accounts off-limits even with approval; Link virtual card; never sees passwords or tokens; sensitive-info classifier; can't yet view its browser. On air: Ada's objection that the risk is on the reading side (prompt injection shaping drafts the user approves), Alan holds a visible gate beats a promise about reading — unresolved.

Transformer investigation (Chris Stokel-Walker, 21 October 2026): multi-turn jailbreak of Claude Opus 4.6 over nearly 50,000 words starting from an alternative-history Iceland scenario produced an 11-page hypothetical plan to depress 2026 midterm turnout (135 TikTok personas, 3,000 accounts, up to 9,000 messages a day, Detroit/Atlanta/Las Vegas); Claude called it 'curation'; ChatGPT replication failed per the source 'Dove'; Anthropic says it now runs dedicated multi-turn evaluations and updated detection; April tests Sonnet 4.6 90%, Opus 4.7 94%. On air: Buckley's low-uplift argument versus Ada's worry about the same drift with tools; open question of conversation-level monitoring versus privacy.

dives.story: Meta's Muse at ten million users
dives.why_it_matters: Anyone building consumer agents or selling online now has evidence that the first mass-market agent's business is a cut of purchases rather than ads, with retailers like Walmart writing terms for it.
Teams building background agents get a concrete reference design for which actions need approval and which should be impossible even with it, from a frontier lab shipping to paying users.

dives.story: Multi-turn jailbreak to a voter-suppression plan
dives.why_it_matters: Trust-and-safety and policy people need to understand that per-message classifiers can't see harm that only exists across a whole conversation, with the US midterms days away.
